key_insight: Global evolutionary search becomes useful in variational quantum algorithms mainly when local optimizers repeatedly fall into inferior basins due to parameter reuse across layers and competing cost terms, not simply because the circuit is deeper.
engineering_relevance: For QAOA and similar VQAs, the result helps decide when the extra evaluation cost of population-based optimization is justified versus when multistart local search is enough.
method: Landscape-first study with controlled QAOA experiments
Compared adaptive differential evolution against multistart BFGS and Powell
Tested mechanisms on unseen spin glasses and standard benchmark Hamiltonians
evidence_signal: Across eight unseen spin glasses, adaptive DE beat both multistart BFGS and Powell on the difficult constructions, and a pre-benchmark landscape score predicted DE’s advantage on 50 new quantum objectives with 80–86% condition-level accuracy.
watch_item: The landscape score is calibrated from confirmation data, so its predictive value may depend on similar problem structure and may not transfer unchanged to arbitrary circuits or hardware-constrained settings.
paper_title: When is global evolutionary search useful for variational quantum algorithms? A landscape-first study
